identity: Neutral gas-phase amidogen NH2, CAS 13770-40-6, bent X 2B1 radical; not NH2- or an NH3 fragment treated as a separate isomer.
recommendation: Prioritize a bounded NH2 candidate comparison: retain the literal inherited thermal fit and its residual while applying the balanced ATcT-minus-JANAF physical D0 shift; compare a NASA-thermal/ATcT alternative separately. Do not silently combine the energy and thermal changes. Keep curated unchanged in this source-review PR.
science: The inherited JANAF energy is less binding than ATcT 1.228 by 4.089 kJ/mol after all H/N atoms are balanced. The JANAF/NASA thermal difference also grows with temperature, so the two candidate constructions are scientifically different. NH2 has the largest elemental footprint among the 33 remaining species, making this a meaningful next replacement calculation. The IUPAC radical assessment (2005) independently reports a much lower molecular formation enthalpy than the older JANAF value, in the direction of ATcT; the accessible NIST CCCBDB transcription was inspected, not the complete IUPAC article.
modern: Andre, Maouhoub-Andre and Rat's June 2026 public thermochemical dataset was inspected in full. It lists three vibrational frequencies, a moment-of-inertia product, symmetry number 2 and a ground electronic weight of 1, with S(298.15 K)=188.940 J/mol/K. That value is about R ln(2) below the NASA/JANAF entropy. The dataset does not make a resolved total-J/fine-structure state-sum convention explicit; a weight of 1 is not by itself proof of an error if spin is included elsewhere. Its electron-spin normalization therefore needs clarification before use. The newer date alone does not establish a better thermal model; the printed energy choices are not a new experimental formation enthalpy. Independent replay of the printed classical-rotation, harmonic-vibration and electronic inputs reproduces Q and S, so an unreported resolved-spin factor is not evident in those printed outputs. A ground-weight-two sensitivity is temperature dependent, and is not an adopted correction.
importance: NH2 connects ammonia and other nitrogen species in hot gas chemistry. The present ideal-gas equilibrium footprint does not assess ammonia photolysis, reaction rates or atmospheric transport.
conventions: The evaluated tables already include their electronic/rotational conventions. No extra electronic factor, symmetry divisor or nuclear-spin factor is applied to JANAF/NASA. A new NH2 state sum must distinguish total J from spin-free rotational N and handle the equivalent H nuclei consistently. Natural-mass evaluated functions are used here; no isotope-resolved mixture is introduced.
followup: Construct the two continuous NH2 candidates with fixed atoms and explicit physical energy/fit-residual bookkeeping; validate G/H/S/Cp and scalar/JAX derivatives, then run current-base network substitutions. Ask the 2026 dataset authors for the ground-spin/rotation convention only if pursuing that thermal alternative; it is not required for the ATcT energy candidate or source-review merge.
